A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OccuFly dataset and camera-based data-generation framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction statistics, CGFormer SSC evaluations, Depth Anything V2 experiments, and reciprocal cross-domain depth-transfer results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original SSC and depth-estimation experiments, reconstruction and pseudo-label evaluations, and an independent annotation-agreement assessment, including additional appendix results.

M1.justification: The SfM/MVS reconstruction, semantic label lifting with voting and kNN, class-aware densification, and frustum-based sampling procedures remain unchanged in substance. Adding depth maps to the sample notation formalizes an existing output. Annotation-grid parameter revisions are experimental-setting changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds semantic-segmentation evaluation using a ConvNeXt comparator trained on seven aerial datasets, while removing v1's explicit Virtual KITTI 2 evaluation branch. OccuFly retains its nine scenes, environments, seasons, and altitudes, but its taxonomy drops FlyingAnimal, reducing coverage from 22 to 21 classes.

E2.justification: The evaluated SSC methods change from CGFormer to Symphonies and DISC, previously only cited. Depth comparisons add MapAnything V1.1, Metric3Dv2, and Depth Anything 3; reconstruction and annotation comparisons additionally evaluate Depth Anything 3, Semantic Segment Anything, and ConvNeXt. DAv2-metric and DAv2-OccuFly are retained under revised names.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises training/validation counts from 14,321/1,997 to 14,804/1,965; the test total remains 3,842, with changed scene-altitude allocations. Annotation-grid spacing changes from fixed 25 m to scene-dependent 23–28 m. New protocols assess reconstruction scale, segmentation mIoU, and pixel agreement against 135 additional annotations excluded from data generation. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of foundation-model reconstruction and automated pseudo-label alternatives, independent geometric/semantic label validation, and environment-wise class-distribution analysis. It removes the reciprocal aerial–Virtual KITTI 2 transfer analysis. Altitude and class-wise SSC analyses remain, but evaluate different models; v1's grouped frequency-normalized performance plot is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance. New agreement percentages and averaged errors are point estimates, not new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: CGFormer results are replaced by Symphonies and DISC results, including overall IoU/mIoU of 13.68%/0.58% and 29.52%/2.04%, respectively, in v2 Table 4. New findings include 526% average reconstruction scale deviation, 17.58% segmentation mIoU, and 92% annotation agreement. Depth-model results expand substantially, while v1 Table 4's altitude-wise DAv2 values are retained in v2 Table 12. These are expanded or replaced evaluations, not demonstrated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical construction and equations remain substantively the same, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation. Correcting the coverage notation from rho(L) to rho(J) and explicitly including existing depth maps in sample notation are clarifications.

C1.justification: The first real-world aerial SSC benchmark and LiDAR-free generation claims remain. However, v2's abstract and contribution list add an explicit central claim of a consistent aerial domain gap across terrestrial SSC models and both 2D and 3D vision foundation models, substantially broadening the claimed scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's favorable interpretation of CGFormer under balanced classes with uniformly difficult aerial SSC and comparatively limited altitude effects. It adds arguments for classical reconstruction and manual annotation, removes the reciprocal-transfer interpretation, and corrects depth overestimation to underestimation. Its new SILog trade-off claim conflicts with Table 5, where both matched models improve after fine-tuning. Static-scene and cross-altitude temporal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 discloses Ingolstadt as the collection region, annotation costs of approximately 29 minutes per image and 1.3 days per scene, and specific variants of added models. Most generation hardware and hyperparameters remain documented. Conversely, the retained Depth Anything V2 experiment loses explicit batch-size and peak-memory information previously provided in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting foundation-model and pseudo-label evaluations and explicitly acknowledges PointSSC as precedent for label lifting, explaining the camera-only aerial adaptation. References tied to Virtual KITTI 2, MobileStereoNet, and Dynamic NeRF disappear. The broader SSC survey and first-aerial-benchmark positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, dataset-evaluation narrative, and benchmark discussion undergo substantial rewriting. The supplement is reorganized to open with scene-level visualizations; depth-dataset comparison moves into the main text, while semantic-taxonomy comparison moves into the appendix. The central method exposition remains largely stable.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the grouped SSC bar chart with a reconstruction comparison, adds an environment-wise frequency chart, and replaces CGFormer qualitative panels with DISC examples. SSC and depth tables are substantially restructured and expanded. Dataset-comparison tables and scene-level visualizations are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the benchmark's evidential foundation: the independent 135-annotation check addresses v1's limited direct validation of label accuracy, while reconstruction alternatives, pseudo-label tests, and broader model comparisons better justify its design and usefulness. These gains outweigh localized reporting regressions, including omitted training details, inconsistent class frequencies between Tables 7 and 11, and the SILog interpretation contradicted by Table 5.
